text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Consensus in Cairo Economic Conference that there are plenty of opportunities for investment and growth in Egypt and the region. Egypt and foreign investors agree on nine megaprojects including export of gas to Turkey at a cost of $4 billion. Germans offer to join in a $5 billion project and the International Monetary Fund forecasts $5 billion in investment to trickle into Egypt until the year 2000.
- President Hosni Mubarak tells CNN: "If there is no progress on the peace process, the situation in the region will explode."
- Head of Israel's industrial union says (Israeli Prime Minister) Benjamin Netanyahu has weakened our chances for cooperation with the Arabs.
- Mubarak tells CNN: "I cannot force the Palestinians to sign a deal that they do not accept."
- The message of the Cairo Economic Conference to the world is that regional cooperation will be realised after advances are made in the peace process.
- Egypt to formally request the re-appointment of (U.N. Secretary-General) Boutrous-Ghali at Monday's Security Council session.
- Heavy rains in southern Egypt. Houses swept away by flash floods but no casualties.

- The Cairo Economic Conference ends today. International recognition for Mubarak's efforts and the economic reforms. Prime Minister Ganzouri says foreign investors offering joint projects with Egypt.
- Four newspapers and television networks interview the President.
- Cassation court cancels sales tax for all companies set up under the new law for investment.
